from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Calculate score: Q dot K.", "Visualize as a heat map.", "Normalize scores using Softmax.", "Scores now sum to one.", "Words get a weighted importance."]
        self.setup_layout("The Math: Dot-Product and Softmax", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        eq = MathTex(r"Q \cdot K^T", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(eq, 'B2', scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(Write(eq))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Creating a simple heatmap effect
        heatmap = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.7, fill_opacity=0.6, fill_color=interpolate_color(BLUE, RED, i/8), stroke_width=0) for i in range(9)]).arrange_in_grid(3, 3)
        self.place_at_grid(heatmap, 'D3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(heatmap))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        softmax_text = MathTex(r"\text{Softmax}", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(softmax_text, 'B5', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(softmax_text))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        matrix_result = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.7, fill_opacity=0.8, fill_color="#7FFF00", stroke_width=1) for i in range(9)]).arrange_in_grid(3, 3)
        self.place_at_grid(matrix_result, 'E3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Transform(heatmap, matrix_result))
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#7FFF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        final_label = Text("Attention Weights", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(final_label, 'A5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(final_label))
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#7FFF00")
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis: Putting it All Together", [
            "Multiply attention weights by values.", 
            "Create context-aware word vectors.", 
            "'It' absorbs 'animal' context."
        ])
        
        # Mobjects
        q_box = Square(side_length=1.0, color="#FF9999")
        k_box = Square(side_length=1.0, color="#99FF99")
        v_box = Square(side_length=1.0, color="#9999FF")
        
        q_label = Text("Q", font_size=24)
        k_label = Text("K", font_size=24)
        v_label = Text("V", font_size=24)
        
        q_group = VGroup(q_box, q_label)
        k_group = VGroup(k_box, k_label)
        v_group = VGroup(v_box, v_label)
        
        central_block = VGroup(q_group, k_group, v_group).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        self.place_at_grid(central_block, 'C3', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        mha_label = Text("Multi-Head Attention", font_size=30, color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(mha_label, 'A3', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF9999"))
        self.play(FadeIn(q_group), FadeIn(k_group), FadeIn(v_group))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#9999FF"))
        self.play(Write(mha_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#99FF99"))
        self.play(Flash(central_block, color="#FFFFFF", flash_radius=1.5, num_lines=12))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Attention Mechanism: How Transformers Read
outline.target_audience: University students with basic programming/math background

sections.title: The Problem: The 'Lost in Translation' Issue
sections.content: Introduce the limitation of previous models (RNNs/LSTMs) which struggle to remember long-range dependencies. Use the concept of 'Contextual Memory' as a prerequisite.
sections.example: In the sentence 'The animal didn't cross the street because it was too tired,' ask: What does 'it' refer to? To know 'it' is the animal, the model must 'pay attention' to the word 'animal' while processing 'it'.

sections.title: The Mechanism: Queries, Keys, and Values (Q, K, V)
sections.content: Use a library analogy to explain Q, K, and V. Query (what I'm looking for), Key (the labels on books), Value (the information in the book). Visualize this as a matching game.
sections.example: Searching for a book in a library: You have a query 'Deep Learning' (Q), matching it against all book labels (K), to retrieve the actual content (V).

sections.title: The Math: Dot-Product and Softmax
sections.content: Explain the attention score calculation: Q dot K^T. Use a heat map visual to show how high dot-product values correspond to stronger 'focus' areas. Normalize using Softmax to create a probability distribution (sum = 1).
sections.example: Visualizing a 3x3 matrix: Word 'it' has a high brightness score (0.8) for 'animal' and low (0.1) for 'street', effectively weighting the importance of each word.

sections.title: Synthesis: Putting it All Together
sections.content: Explain how the model creates a new, context-aware representation of each word by multiplying the Attention Weights with the Values (V).
sections.example: The word 'it' is no longer just a pronoun; it is now a mathematical vector that has 'absorbed' the meaning of 'animal' from the surrounding context.

sections.title: Conclusion: Why This Changes Everything
sections.content: Summarize that attention allows parallel processing (unlike RNNs) and creates global context, enabling LLMs to understand complex relationships in massive datasets.
sections.example: Comparing a slow reader (RNN) reading word-by-word, versus a Transformer (Attention) that sees the whole page at once and highlights the most important connections simultaneously.
